title: firecrawl /firecrawl
summary: 🔥 Firecrawl Knowledge infrastructure to make your agents smarter. 🔥 You can use Firecrawl three ways. This repo holds the code for Firecrawl Local and the self-hosted server, along with SDKs that work with all three. Firecrawl Local . Run Firecrawl on your own machine as one binary that turns websites into clean markdown, plugs into your AI agent as an MCP server and serves the Firecrawl API on localhost. Firecrawl Cloud . Use the hosted service at firecrawl.dev for everything Local does at scale with nothing to run, plus search and the 550+ data providers in Firecrawl Alexandria for far more knowledge than scraping alone. Self-hosting . Deploy the full Firecrawl server from apps/api with its own queues, workers and databases on your own infrastructure. Pst. Hey, you, join our stargazers :) Firecrawl Local Firecrawl Local scrapes, crawls and maps from your own machine without a database, queue or container, and it reaches Firecrawl Cloud when your AI agents need search or Alexandria. It installs from crates.io. You need Rust and a C compiler, which on macOS means xcode-select --install and on Debian or Ubuntu means build-essential . cargo install firecrawl-local If you don't have Rust, Firecrawl Cloud runs the same scrape with nothing to build and no signup. npx -y firecrawl-cli@latest scrape https://firecrawl.dev Scrape a page and print its markdown. firecrawl-local scrape https://firecrawl.dev --markdown Crawl a site and save one markdown file per page. firecrawl-local crawl https://docs.firecrawl.dev --limit 50 --out ./pages List every URL on a site. firecrawl-local map https://firecrawl.dev Pages that need JavaScript render in the Chrome or Chromium already on your machine, and PDFs and Office documents are parsed locally too. Without a browser, static pages still work and a page that needed one comes back with a warning. Add it to your AI agent init finds Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, Gemini CLI and Codex on your machine and adds Firecrawl Loca

title: Context Scaling: A New Frontier of AI Scaling
summary:
arXiv:2611.33160v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Many failures of deployed AI arise not from weak inference but from a mismatch between the state a task depends on and the context available when the system acts. Relevant user state, repository revisions, tool traces, sensor readings, or environment changes may be unavailable, distorted, or poorly selected. We call the effort to reduce this bottleneck context scaling. We frame a model as $P_\theta(d\mid c)$ within a system governed by three budgets: training $B_\theta$, decision-time $B_d$, and context-infrastructure $B_c$. Pretraining scaling invests in $\theta$; decision-time scaling searches, refines, or verifies decisions under supplied context; context scaling improves the system's capacity to acquire, represent, deliver, evaluate, and persist deployment state for model use. The three programs interact, but only $B_c$ targets what the system can make available before a decision. This view makes the model-infrastructure pair the unit of analysis. We define effective-context value as a task- and intervention-dependent attribution, separate deployment state from model-visible context, and identify availability, fidelity, selection, and utilization failures. We then organize current mechanisms through a five-operation context lifecycle and propose controlled budget interventions and utility-cost curves for evaluation. The resulting agenda centers on grounded reporting, interaction-data and full-cost infrastructure, and safety and governance for persistent, adaptive systems.
title_es: Context Scaling: una nueva frontera en escalado de sistemas de IA
bajada: Un nuevo paper propone 'context scaling' como un área crítica de investigación en IA, enfocándose en cómo los sistemas acceden, representan y persisten el estado de despliegue. Esta perspectiva complementa los enfoques tradicionales de escalado de modelos y tiempo de decisión.
bajada_en: A new paper proposes 'context scaling' as a critical research area in AI, focusing on how systems acquire, represent, and persist deployment state. This perspective complements traditional model and decision-time scaling approaches.

title: MGMem: An Efficient, Deterministic, and Provenance-Preserving Framework for Long-Horizon Agent Memory
summary:
arXiv:2611.33174v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-horizon Large Language Model (LLM) agents need persistent memory that surfaces the right past interaction at the right time across thousands of turns. Many systems index by invoking generative LLMs to rewrite history into summaries, facts, or knowledge graphs--a step that is (a) costly (thousands of generative calls per build), (b) non-deterministic (undermining reproducibility and giving inconsistent answers across runs), and (c) provenance-erasing (the reader sees synthesized text, not the original turn). We propose MGMem, a framework with no generative indexing calls that replaces this step with a deterministic discriminative-parser pipeline: recurring mentions across sessions are organized into an incidence graph, question mentions are resolved by a subject-conditioned three-stage resolver, and raw dialogue episodes are returned to the reader. On English multi-session dialogue QA, MGMem outperforms matched-protocol baselines on LoCoMo without generative indexing calls; on the full LongMemEval-S, it remains competitive overall and leads or ties on single-session types among local retrieval comparisons. Code: https://github.com/junhong-h/MGMem
title_es: MGMem: memoria determinística para agentes LLM de largo horizonte
bajada: Un framework determinístico que mejora la memoria persistente de agentes LLM sin usar costosas llamadas generativas para indexing. Preserva la provenance y es reproducible, resolviendo problemas críticos en sistemas de IA de larga duración.
bajada_en: A deterministic framework that improves persistent memory for LLM agents without expensive generative indexing calls. It preserves provenance and is reproducible, solving critical issues in long-horizon AI systems.

title: AutoformBench: A Lean Formalization Benchmark for Advanced Mathematics
summary:
arXiv:2611.33165v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AI systems are increasingly capable of producing machine-checked Lean proofs of advanced mathematical results. Real mathematical formalization, however, is not isolated theorem proving: it requires building the definitions and intermediate lemmas that connect a result to a formal library. Existing evaluations often provide isolated theorem statements in settings where much of this supporting theory is already available in Mathlib. We introduce AutoformBench, a benchmark of 341 Lean 4 formalization tasks drawn from 24 advanced mathematical sources. Lean-experienced mathematicians formalized and audited each target statement, leaving the corresponding Lean proof to the evaluated agent. Each problem is embedded in a broader mathematical development: agents receive the informal proof but must translate it into Lean while constructing the missing definitions, intermediate lemmas, and supporting infrastructure. We compare the performance of frontier models on these problems. We find a largely shared difficulty frontier: success depends less on mathematical domain than on models' ability to construct missing formal infrastructure. Data and code at https://github.com/facebookresearch/autoformbench
title_es: AutoformBench: benchmark de formalización de matemáticas avanzadas
bajada: Se introduce un benchmark de 341 tareas de formalización en Lean 4 basadas en matemáticas reales avanzadas, donde los modelos deben construir la infraestructura formal faltante. Los resultados revelan que la capacidad de construir definiciones e lemas intermedios es más crítica que el dominio matemático.
bajada_en: A benchmark of 341 Lean 4 formalization tasks from advanced mathematics is introduced, where models must construct missing formal infrastructure. Results show that building definitions and intermediate lemmas is more critical than mathematical domain.

title: What, Who, and When: Structured Harm Assessment for Mental Health Safety via Short Reasoning
summary:
arXiv:2611.33263v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The growing use of large language models (LLMs) for mental health support raises important safety concerns. Existing guard models primarily identify categories of harmful content, often overlooking the context needed to determine an appropriate response. We introduce a clinically grounded taxonomy that characterizes harm along three dimensions: what the harm is, who is involved, and when it occurs. It further separates harm characterization from intervention decisions, thus enabling safety policies to be specified outside the model weights through explicit, clinician-curated instructions that can be updated and audited. We validate the taxonomy with expert clinicians and validate a panel of LLM judges to scale annotation. Relabeling public benchmarks in this taxonomy shows that they rarely contain harm directed at the user, which accounts for nearly half of the harm in real conversations. We then train MindGuard2, a 35B-A3B reasoning-based guard model using supervised fine-tuning on short reasoning traces followed by reinforcement learning with a reasoning-length penalty, to minimize inference overhead while preserving the benefits of reasoning. On two public benchmarks and real-world conversations, MindGuard2 achieves balanced accuracy comparable to the substantially larger GLM-5.3 at approximately 10x lower median latency, advancing the accuracy-latency Pareto frontier. Furthermore, it achieves low false-positive rates at high recall, helping balance the need to detect unsafe situations against the risk of unnecessary interventions that may disrupt support and undermine user trust. We release a safety guardrail model with SOTA performance trained on synthetic data, together with synthetic conversations and annotations of public benchmarks in our taxonomy.
title_es: MindGuard2: evaluación estructurada de daño para seguridad en salud mental
bajada: Se presenta una taxonomía clínica para evaluar daño en LLMs usados para soporte mental, separando caracterización de daño de decisiones de intervención. MindGuard2 es un modelo de guardia de 35B que preserva seguridad con overhead bajo.
bajada_en: A clinical taxonomy for assessing harm in LLMs used for mental health support is presented, separating harm characterization from intervention decisions. MindGuard2 is a 35B guard model that preserves safety with low overhead.

title: Verified experience improves materials prediction with large language models
summary:
arXiv:2611.33195v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Materials discovery is an iterative loop: experiments and calculations verify predictions, and each outcome can inform the next. Yet most predictors are specialized single-task models fixed after training. Large language models have recently emerged as predictors across heterogeneous tasks but generally underperform specialized models, and retrieval-augmented variants discard their own outcomes. Benchmarks also score queries in isolation, leaving improvement from outcomes untested. Here we construct MatMemBench, a sequential benchmark of 22 materials tasks that reveals outcomes only after prediction and tests online adaptation, memory retention and cross-task transfer. We present MatRecall, a framework that lets large language models store verified predictions, with evidence, outcome and error, as episodes and recall them without retraining. MatRecall improved median performance by 62% over a memory-free model, exceeded specialized models on 11 tasks, remained useful after feedback stopped and transferred between related tasks. Verified experience could become a reusable resource for self-improving discovery loops.
title_es: MatRecall: LLMs que mejoran predicciones con experiencia verificada
bajada: Un framework que permite a LLMs almacenar y recordar predicciones verificadas en descubrimiento de materiales, mejorando rendimiento un 62% mediano. Demuestra transferencia entre tareas y potencial para loops de auto-mejora.
bajada_en: A framework enabling LLMs to store and recall verified predictions in materials discovery, improving median performance by 62%. Demonstrates cross-task transfer and potential for self-improving loops.

title: Constraint-Aware Test-Time Scoring for LLM and VLM Candidate Selection
summary:
arXiv:2611.33161v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: When an LLM or VLM produces several candidate answers, picking the best one usually relies on the model's own confidence, a learned judge model, or a domain check. Each has a known weakness: an answer can be fluent but insecure, mathematically plausible but physically infeasible, or rated highly by a judge while quietly breaking a task requirement. We propose a scoring framework that combines a small set of hard checks every answer must pass with a wider set of softer checks whose scores are blended into one number per candidate. This adaptive scoring framework consists of three components: a drafting model that produces the candidates, a configuring model that selects and weights the checks for each task, and scoring models that rate properties no grounded tool can compute. We apply our proposed method to four tasks: writing code that is both correct and secure (CWEval), generating robot manipulation plans (LIBERO with added safety variants), passing competitive-programming hidden tests (LiveCodeBench), and answering questions from retrieved documents (HotpotQA). An ablation study isolates the contribution of each component and finds that the largest gains come from combining hard checks with candidate comparison: on tasks where the first sampled answer is often broken or unsafe, this pairing lifts joint correctness-and-safety by up to +0.21 (retrieval-augmented QA) and code-generation safety by up to +0.28 (CWEval), with the size of the gain tracking how weak the first sample is, falling to near zero or slightly negative where it is already strong. The per-task layer that selects and weights the softer checks adds no measurable value over simpler alternatives. This builds a unified scoring framework, together with an ablation that identifies the grounded hard checks, not the soft-factor configuration, as the source of the gain.
title_es: Scoring con restricciones para selección de candidatos en LLM y VLM
bajada: Un framework que combina verificaciones duras con validaciones suaves para elegir la mejor respuesta entre candidatos de LLM/VLM. Se valida en tareas como generación segura de código, robotics y competitive programming.
bajada_en: A framework combining hard checks with soft validations to select the best answer from LLM/VLM candidates. Validated on tasks including secure code generation, robotics, and competitive programming.

title: Feature-Based Explainability of Transformer Scoring Models: A Fidelity-First Framework for Automated Writing Assessment
summary:
arXiv:2611.33175v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Transformer-based automated writing scoring models can achieve strong agreement with human scores while providing limited transparency into the response characteristics associated with their predictions. This study evaluated a feature-based post-hoc explanation approach in which explanatory fidelity was established before feature importance was interpreted. English Language Arts responses from three writing prompts in Grades 6 and 8 were analyzed, with about 12,700 responses per prompt and separate DeBERTa-v3-base research models for Expression and Conventions. Each response was represented by 61 interpretable linguistic and writing-quality features. Four approaches - theory-driven composites, hierarchical feature groupings, exploratory factor analysis, and Random Forest surrogates - were compared in their ability to reproduce DeBERTa predictions. Random Forest surrogates produced the largest observed R2 values across all six prompt-by-trait conditions, with held-out R2 values from .81 to .95. SHAP analyses showed substantial overlap in high-importance features across traits, with 75% to 90% of the top 20 features shared. Trait differentiation occurred mainly through relative feature weighting: Expression showed greater importance for lexical and conceptual indicators, whereas Conventions showed greater importance for sentence-level and syntactic-control indicators. Under researcher-defined mappings, rubric correspondence was 90%-95% for Expression and 12%-18% for Conventions. These percentages are descriptive and conditional on the mappings and available linguistic features. The findings support a fidelity-first framework for examining apparent scoring priorities while distinguishing post-hoc evidence about model behavior from direct explanation of transformer internals.
title_es: Explicabilidad de modelos Transformer para evaluación automática de escritura
bajada: Un framework de explicabilidad basado en features usando Random Forest surrogates logra alta fidelidad (R² de .81 a .95) al reproducir predicciones de modelos DeBERTa-v3. Facilita la interpretabilidad en sistemas de calificación automática.
bajada_en: An explainability framework using Random Forest surrogates achieves high fidelity (R² .81 to .95) in reproducing DeBERTa-v3 predictions. It enables interpretability in automated writing assessment systems.

title: Psychophysics of Duration Perception in Multimodal Large Language Models
summary:
arXiv:2611.33176v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Studies of time perception in language models focus mainly on text-based settings. Yet multimodal models are increasingly used for tasks that require perceiving the passage of time, making the limits of their temporal perception important to understand. We measure the limits of duration perception from audio against a human baseline to address this gap. Drawing from psychophysics, we operationalise duration perception as a melody recognition task, testing when a melody becomes unrecognisable as it is slowed down. Of 21 tested models, most cannot recognise well-known melodies without labelled in-context examples. With in-context examples, seven recognise melodies reliably, most peaking within the median human recognition band. Generalisation is limited: (i) recognition peaks shift with in-context example speed, (ii) melody titles induce prediction bias, and (iii) providing examples with scientific pitch notation does not prevent accuracy declining at long note durations for most models. In humans, the recognition window is a property of the perceiver; in current models, it is largely a property of the prompt.
title_es: Percepción de duración en modelos multimodales: límites psicofísicos
bajada: Un estudio mide cómo modelos multimodales perciben duraciones de audio comparados con humanos, usando recognition de melodías. Revela limitaciones significativas: la ventana de reconocimiento depende del prompt, no de capacidades inherentes.
bajada_en: A study measures how multimodal models perceive audio durations compared to humans using melody recognition tasks. It reveals significant limitations: the recognition window depends on the prompt, not inherent capabilities.

title: General-Purpose Decision Models for AI Configuration Tuning
summary:
arXiv:2611.33190v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AI configuration tuning searches for settings that improve the performance of AI systems under a limited budget. Existing tuners use different sampling and search policies, making the choice of decision strategy central to both tuning quality and cost. We investigate whether general-purpose decision models can guide tuning, using Jev as a deployed representative that returns structured choices and numeric scores across diverse tasks. To assess where it helps, we compare its use as an optimizer, performance predictor, and region guider against conventional methods and a large language model (LLM) on eight AI tuning tasks. Conventional optimizers attain rank 1 in six of eight comparisons. Similarly, established predictors outperform Jev in seven. Through region guidance, however, it finds configurations with lower perplexity than those selected by the native tuner, offering a quality gain when additional decision time and API fees are acceptable. These findings yield actionable recommendations on selecting the decision role, retaining conventional predictors, and balancing tuning quality against cost.
title_es: Modelos de decisión para auto-tuning de configuraciones de sistemas de IA
bajada: Un estudio evalúa si modelos de decisión general-propósito pueden guiar tuning de configuraciones en sistemas de IA bajo presupuesto limitado. Los resultados muestran que métodos convencionales siguen siendo superiores en la mayoría de casos.
bajada_en: A study evaluates whether general-purpose decision models can guide AI system configuration tuning under limited budgets. Results show conventional methods remain superior in most cases.
